provenance.question: do different admissible thetas (same training plan, different weights) generalise differently? i.e. is the max-margin vertex a good selection rule?
provenance.admissibility: measured, not assumed: the reference theta does NOT make the training plan optimal (its decoded map is wrong at thousands of vertices and its exact regret is ~1% of R_uniform). Admissibility is therefore defined RELATIVE to the shipped reference: regret <= R(reference) * (1 + slack_rel) -- 'equally good on the training pair'
provenance.why_relative: an absolute criterion was tried first and is empty at the reference, so it would have reported 'one point' for the wrong reason. The discrete test (decoded map == identity) is reported alongside as the honest strength of the certificate
provenance.sampler: normalised Gaussian random walk from the fitted vertex; only feasible proposals are kept, so every scored theta certifies the SAME plan
provenance.metric: geodesic miss@5% on the 8 held-out pairs; the spread across admitted thetas is the diagnostic
provenance.go_no_go: GO if the spread exceeds ~0.01 (the seed-to-seed noise) and the max-margin point is not near the top; NO-GO if every admitted theta scores within noise
